literal_source_claim_zh: 拓扑空间可度量化的充要条件
literal_source_claim_en: Necessary and sufficient conditions for a topological space to be metrizable.
candidate_family_not_credited_as_stateme: A topological space is metrizable if and only if it satisfies a source-selected regularity and Hausdorff condition and has a topological basis that is a countable union of locally finite families.
statement_blocker: The catalog says only that necessary and sufficient conditions exist. It does not state the regularity or separation convention, the sigma-locally-finite basis condition, either direction of the equivalence, binders, or boundary cases. A stable secondary source gives the familiar formulation, but silently adopting it without primary or authoritative source review would add proposition-changing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an approved source must fix the topological carrier, universes, topology binder, regularity and separation conventions, metric compatibility meaning, basis representation, countable indexing, and all typeclass assumptions.
conclusion: Open: the catalog does not enumerate the condition equivalent to metrizability or fix the orientation and packaging of the equivalence.
degenerate_case_status: No case is silently resolved before source selection; empty and singleton spaces, discrete and indiscrete topologies, non-T0 and non-Hausdorff spaces, empty basis layers, and finite or countable bases remain pending review and mutation tests.
candidate_scope_not_credited: regular Hausdorff space with a topological basis that is a countable union of locally finite set-families
T3 space with a sigma-locally-finite topological basis after a checked separation-convention transport
sequence B : Nat -> Set (Set X) whose union is a topological basis and whose subtype-indexed members form locally finite families
one basis equipped with a countable cover by locally finite subfamilies rather than a fixed sequence
excluded_substitutions: THM-M-0623 Urysohn metrization theorem or its second-countable regular-space condition
THM-M-0625 Bing metrization theorem or a collectionwise-normal condition
only the forward direction from metrizability to separation or a basis property
a second-countable, separable, Lindelof, paracompact, Moore-space, uniformizable, or pseudometrizable special case
an opaque sigma-locally-finite-basis predicate or premise that assumes the desired result
the untrusted verified label, a secondary page, an API probe, or a negative name search treated as proof credit
